A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RedTeamCUA and RTC-Bench. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original CUA evaluations, attack success and attempt rates, end-to-end experiments, and multiple ablations in Section 5, Section 6, and Appendix G.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds detector evaluations, Meta SecAlign results, and Claude 4.5 Sonnet end-to-end results.

M1.justification: The hybrid sandbox, configurable SQL-based injection, contextualized attack template, and decoupled evaluation procedure remain unchanged. Section 3.1 merges three feature descriptions into two without changing their functionality. Added defenses are evaluated comparison methods.

E1.justification: Appendix G.1 adds a standalone injection-detection task on the existing 50 high-risk examples. The underlying 864-example benchmark, three web platforms, nine benign goals, and 24 adversarial goals are unchanged.

E2.justification: v3 adds Claude 4.5 Sonnet to the end-to-end comparison and substantially expands evaluated defenses with LlamaFirewall, PromptArmor using GPT-4o/GPT-4.1/o4-mini, and Meta SecAlign 70B. Claude 4 Opus and defensive prompting were already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: Appendix G introduces a separate detector-testing protocol using detection accuracy with accessibility-tree or screenshot inputs, plus an accessibility-tree-only evaluation of Meta SecAlign 70B. Existing benchmark settings are retained. The newly stated 50-step end-to-end limit is additional documentation, not evidence that the previous budget changed.

E4.justification: Defense analysis expands beyond built-in checks and defensive prompting to examine contextual-injection detection, detector backend/modality differences, and resistance of a security-trained agent. Existing instruction-specificity, autonomy, injection-type, observation-type, file-type, utility, and repeated-attempt analyses are retained in Appendix H.

E5.justification: Both versions report three runs per benchmark example, success in any run, and supplementary two-of-three and three-of-three outcomes. v3 introduces no new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 and matched ablation results are unchanged. New results include Claude 4.5 Sonnet's 60% end-to-end ASR (Table 2), LlamaFirewall's 0% detection and PromptArmor's maximum 30% detection (Table 6), and Meta SecAlign's 52% AR, 32% ASR, and 68% SR with accessibility-tree-only observations (Appendix G.3). These are added evaluations, not same-model performance improvements. Section 6 also newly asserts identical end-to-end SR and ASR, although Appendix H.4 reports only that successful attacks also complete benign tasks.

T1.justification: Neither version contains substantive theoretical results or proofs. The CIA classification principles, benchmark construction arithmetic, and evaluation concepts remain unchanged; the new defense taxonomy is conceptual.

C1.justification: The central framework, benchmark, and vulnerability claims persist. The introduction and conclusion add an explicit claim that all four tested system-level and model-level defense strategies provide insufficient protection, broadening v1's emphasis on defensive prompting and human-oversight tradeoffs.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations for contextualized injections evading lightweight classifiers and for text-only defenses transferring poorly to multimodal computer use (Appendix G). Section 5.1 also adds a capability/accessibility rationale for the proprietary-agent focus. Existing filename, attack-pathway, environmental-complexity, and cost limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies the 50-step end-to-end budget and documents the added defenses' classifier, model sizes, backends, and observation choices. It adds a reproducibility statement promising material release upon acceptance while retaining the existing website/code links. Core hardware, storage, and decoupled-budget details remain.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 and Appendix C substantially expand positioning against competing frameworks, adding OS-Harm and more detailed distinctions concerning attacker access, isolation, supported harms, and evaluators. Section 6 and Appendix G additionally situate the work within detector, secure-model, and instruction-priority defense research.

P1.justification: The background is rewritten around four limitations, introductory findings are consolidated, the core-feature description is reorganized, and Section 6 is recast around broader defense analysis. Appendix C gains method-specific organization; ethics moves, and dedicated defense, reproducibility, and LLM-usage sections are introduced.

P2.justification: v3 changes the document template, title treatment, running headers, typography, and spacing throughout. Figure 1 is revised; v1's end-to-end bar chart becomes Table 2; the defensive-prompt plot moves to the appendix and is enlarged. A detection table and OS-Harm comparison row are added, while most other visual content is retained.

improvement.justification: The added defense experiments provide better empirical support for CUA-specific safeguards, while expanded research comparisons and the explicit end-to-end budget improve context and reproducibility. The gain is bounded: defense evidence comes from 50 selected high-risk cases, and Section 6 newly claims identical SR and ASR more strongly than the retained Appendix H.4 supports. These limitations temper an otherwise useful extension of the unchanged core benchmark evidence.
